title: Cold rebuild: the top N pipeline
summary: Run sort | uniq -c | sort -rn on real logs from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Text pipelines* you built the **top N** pipeline, `sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head`,
on real logs. Now do it again from memory: the same machine and data, **no hints, no solution to peek at**.
The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; typing them cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Which grep shows only the **uncommented, non-blank** lines of a config file?
steps.explain: `-v` inverts a pattern matching comment lines (`^#`) or empty lines (`^$`). Option 3 would also drop lines with a `#` in the middle, like `url=http://x/#a`.

steps.title: The top N pipeline, cold
prompt: The logs are in `~/logs` again. Write each answer into `~/answers/` (create it first):
1. `top-paths.txt`: the 5 most requested paths in `access.log` with their counts, biggest first, as `sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5` prints them. The path is field 6 when you split on spaces.
2. `statuses.txt`: every status code (field 8) with its count, biggest first.
3. `top-failer.txt`: just the name of the user with the most `login_failed` events in `events.jsonl`, one JSON object per line.
From memory: no hints this time.
